## Complete HomeKit support for the UniFi Access ecosystem using [Homebridge](https://homebridge.io).
</DIV>
</SPAN>
<!-- MASTHEAD:END -->

`homebridge-unifi-access` is a [Homebridge](https://homebridge.io) plugin that provides HomeKit support to the [UniFi Access](https://ui.com/door-access) device ecosystem. [UniFi Access](https://ui.com/door-access) is [Ubiquiti's](https://www.ui.com) door access security platform, with doorbell, reader, lock, and controller hardware options for you to choose from, as well as an app which you can use to view, configure and manage your door access security.

### MQTT Support

[MQTT](https://mqtt.org) is a popular Internet of Things (IoT) messaging protocol that can be used to weave together different smart devices and orchestrate or instrument them in an infinite number of ways. In short - it lets things that might not normally be able to talk to each other communicate across ecosystems, provided they can support MQTT.

I've provided MQTT support for those that are interested - I'm genuinely curious, if not a bit skeptical, at how many people actually want to use this capability. MQTT has a lot of nerd-credibility, and it was a fun side project to mess around with. :smile:

`homebridge-unifi-access` will publish MQTT events if you've configured a broker in the controller-specific settings. The plugin supports a rich set of capabilities over MQTT. This includes:

  * Doorbell ring events.
  * Lock events, including triggering locks via MQTT.
  * Door position sensor (DPS) events.
  * Terminal input events (REL, REN, REX).
  * Tamper status events for hubs with tamper detection.
  * Unlock attribution - who unlocked a door and how. See [unlock attribution](#unlock-attribution) for additional details.
  * Side door events for UA Gate devices.
  * Raw telemetry publishing.

### Configuration

This documentation assumes you know what MQTT is, what an MQTT broker does, and how to configure it. Setting up an MQTT broker is beyond the scope of this documentation. There are plenty of guides available on how to do so just a search away.

You configure MQTT through the feature options webUI, at the scope of the controller whose events you want published: select that controller in the sidebar and set the two options below. The settings are:

| Feature Option        | Description
|-----------------------|----------------------------------
| `Mqtt.Url`            | The URL of your MQTT broker. **This must be in URL form**, e.g.: `mqtt://user:password@1.2.3.4`.
| `Mqtt.Topic`          | The base topic to publish to. The default is: `unifi/access`.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Mqtt.Url** must be a valid URL. Just entering a hostname will result in an error. The URL can use any of these protocols: `mqtt`, `mqtts`, `tcp`, `tls`, `ws`, `wss`.

A `controller` configuration block may also carry `mqttUrl` and `mqttTopic` properties directly. That is the legacy form of these same two settings: the plugin reads a property whenever no feature option answers for that controller, and the first time you open this plugin's settings in the Homebridge webUI each property is moved into the controller-scoped feature option that supersedes it. There is nothing for you to do about it - a configuration nobody opens keeps working on the properties it already has.

When events are published, by default, the topics look like:

> ```sh
> unifi/access/1234567890AB/lock
> unifi/access/ABCDEF123456/doorbell
> unifi/access/AABBCCDDEE02-PORT1/lock
> ```

In the above examples, `1234567890AB`, `ABCDEF123456`, and `AABBCCDDEE02-PORT1` are device identities - the identity `homebridge-unifi-access` shows for each of your devices in the homebridge log on startup and in its webUI. A device's identity is its serial number: the hardware MAC address without separators, in uppercase, with the port qualifier appended for a port of a UniFi Access Enterprise hub (`-PORT1` in the example above). We use MAC addresses as an easy way to guarantee unique identifiers that won't change. Additionally, you can use the UniFi Access app or webUI to lookup what the MAC addresses are of your devices, should you need to do so.

### <A NAME="publish"></A>Topics Published

The topics and messages that `homebridge-unifi-access` publishes are:

<!-- MQTT PUBLISHED:BEGIN - Auto-generated by homebridge-plugin-utils. Do not edit this region by hand. -->
#### Door and Lock Topics

| Topic       | Access Device Type                                                        | Message Published
|-------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------
| `doorbell`  | Hub with a doorbell                                                       | `true` when ringing, `false` when the ring ends.
| `dps`       | Access Enterprise hub ports, UA Gate, UA Hub, UA Hub Door Mini, UA Ultra  | `true` when open, `false` when closed, `unknown` if not wired. The door position sensor.
| `lock`      | All hubs                                                                  | `true` when locked, `false` when unlocked.
| `rel`       | UA Hub                                                                    | `true` when open, `false` when closed. The remote release sensor.
| `ren`       | UA Hub                                                                    | `true` when open, `false` when closed. The request to enter sensor.
| `rex`       | UA Hub, UA Hub Door Mini, UA Ultra                                        | `true` when open, `false` when closed. The request to exit sensor.
| `tamper`    | Hub with tamper detection                                                 | `true` when tampering is detected, `false` when it is no longer detected, `unknown` when tampering alerts are turned off on the controller. The tamper status.
| `unlock`    | All hubs                                                                  | A JSON describing who unlocked the door and how. See [Unlock Attribution](#unlock-attribution) for additional documentation. Published only when `Controller.Webhooks` is enabled.

#### Side Door Topics (UA Gate Only)

| Topic              | Access Device Type  | Message Published
|--------------------|---------------------|----------------------------------
| `sidedoor/dps`     | UA Gate             | `true` when open, `false` when closed, `unknown` if not wired. The side door (pedestrian gate) position sensor.
| `sidedoor/lock`    | UA Gate             | `true` when locked, `false` when unlocked. The side door lock state.
| `sidedoor/unlock`  | UA Gate             | A JSON describing who unlocked the side door and how. See [Unlock Attribution](#unlock-attribution) for additional documentation. Published only when `Controller.Webhooks` is enabled.

#### Telemetry Topics

| Topic        | Access Device Type  | Message Published
|--------------|---------------------|----------------------------------
| `telemetry`  | Controller          | All UniFi Access telemetry from the realtime events API. This is the raw feed - you're on your own to parse through it for the messages you may be interested in. This is published to the controller's identity rather than a device's: the controller's serial number in the same form as a device identity, or the configured address of a controller reached with an API token alone. Published only when `Controller.Publish.Telemetry` is enabled.

<!-- MQTT PUBLISHED:END -->

Messages are published to MQTT when an action occurs on an Access device that triggers the respective event, or when an MQTT message is received for one of the topics `homebridge-unifi-access` subscribes to.

### <A NAME="subscribe"></A>Topics Subscribed

The topics that `homebridge-unifi-access` subscribes to are:

<!-- MQTT SUBSCRIBED:BEGIN - Auto-generated by homebridge-plugin-utils. Do not edit this region by hand. -->
#### Door and Lock Topics

| Topic           | Access Device Type                                                        | Message Expected
|-----------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------
| `doorbell/get`  | Hub with a doorbell                                                       | `true` will trigger a publish event of the current doorbell ring status.
| `dps/get`       | Access Enterprise hub ports, UA Gate, UA Hub, UA Hub Door Mini, UA Ultra  | `true` will trigger a publish event of the current door position sensor state.
| `lock/get`      | All hubs                                                                  | `true` will trigger a publish event of the current lock state.
| `lock/set`      | All hubs                                                                  | `true` to lock, `false` to unlock. On hubs other than UA Gate, locking requires a configured lock delay interval - a door left on the default momentary unlock has no relock to perform, and the request is refused with an error in the log.

#### Side Door Topics (UA Gate Only)

| Topic                | Access Device Type  | Message Expected
|----------------------|---------------------|----------------------------------
| `sidedoor/dps/get`   | UA Gate             | `true` will trigger a publish event of the current side door position sensor state.
| `sidedoor/lock/get`  | UA Gate             | `true` will trigger a publish event of the current side door lock state.
| `sidedoor/lock/set`  | UA Gate             | `true` to lock, `false` to unlock. This controls the side door lock relay.

<!-- MQTT SUBSCRIBED:END -->

### <A NAME="unlock-attribution"></A>Unlock Attribution

Most topics above carry a simple value, because most of them report a state. An unlock is different: it has an author. When the controller can tell the plugin who opened a door and how they were credentialed, that arrives over a webhook delivery rather than the realtime event socket, and the plugin republishes it to the `unlock` topic - or `sidedoor/unlock` for the side door of a UA Gate.

These topics require `Controller.Webhooks` to be enabled, which in turn requires an API token. Refused attempts are reported here too, so `result` is what tells you whether the door actually opened.

`homebridge-unifi-access` will publish a JSON in the following format:

> ```js
> { "actor": "Jane Doe", "actorType": "user", "method": "NFC", "policy": "Business Hours", "reader": "d8b3706bb73b", "result": "Access Granted", "time": "2026-08-15 16:09:58 -0500 CDT" }
> ```

| Property          | Description
|-------------------|----------------------------------
| `actor`           | The name of whoever unlocked the door, or `null` when the controller attributed it to no one.
| `actorType`       | What kind of actor that was, or `null` when unattributed.
| `method`          | How the door was addressed, as the controller's own token - `NFC`, `CALL`, `WAVE`, and `REMOTE_THROUGH_UAH` are the ones seen so far, and the controller may send others.
| `policy`          | The access policy that governed the unlock, or `null` when none did.
| `reader`          | The identifier of the reader that took the credential, or `null` when no reader was involved.
| `result`          | Whether access was granted or refused.
| `time`            | When the controller recorded the unlock, spelled the way the controller spells it rather than as an ISO timestamp.

> [!NOTE]
>   * MQTT support is disabled by default. It's enabled when an MQTT broker is specified in the configuration.
>   * MQTT is configured per-controller. This allows you to have different MQTT brokers for different Access controllers, if needed.
>   * If connectivity to the broker is lost, it will perpetually retry to connect in one-minute intervals.
>   * If a bad URL is provided, MQTT support will not be enabled.
